done_state: tessera/tessguard/ provides a non-blocking, on-demand-only coverage audit (real DB events, repo-scoped Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit + subagent transcripts, binary zero/nonzero over a completed session) and a genuinely blocking git pre-commit/pre-push hard gate (real DB events, 24h window), both operating purely through store's existing public methods with zero changes to store/api/gitops/reviewui/common, demonstrated against real fixtures and this repo's own real data.

criteria.statement: project_resolve.resolve_projects_for_repo/resolve_projects_for_cwd return a list (never a singular/None on multi-match) and correctly include every registered project sharing one source_root, using os.sep-aware path-component matching -- never a bare str.startswith.

event_activity.REAL_TESSERA_WRITE_EVENT_TYPES is exactly {TicketCreated, CommentAdded, StatusChanged, TicketCriteriaFrozen, ClaimRecorded}; project attribution is derived from each event's ticket_id prefix with a guard against NULL ticket_id before the split (never an unguarded rsplit).

transcript.iter_write_tool_calls enumerates Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit calls scoped via realpath to the repo's own root, plus subagent transcripts at <hyphenated-path>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl, and never Bash.

audit.audit_session computes a binary predicate (real in-repo edit activity exists AND zero real TESSERA-write events exist for the repo's registered project(s), any-of across multiple projects) -- not a ratio, no threshold.

The named transcript is accepted if EITHER its first recorded cwd is under the audited root OR it contains real in-repo edits; rejected as invalid input (a distinct, non-clean outcome) only when neither holds -- never silently treated as a clean zero-edit session.

The DB path is resolved absolutely and existence-checked before Store() is called; a missing or unreachable DB path produces a distinct non-clean audit-log outcome, never conflated with a real zero-registered-projects clean result (Store() silently creating an empty DB must not read as coverage-confirmed).

run_periodic_audit never exits non-zero for a flagged result, and tessguard is never referenced anywhere in .claude/settings.json's hook registration -- non-blocking by construction, not by convention.
criteria.verification: python3 -m unittest tessera.tessguard.tests.test_audit.AuditTests.test_flagged_result_exits_zero exits 0; grep -c tessguard /Users/m5/dev/ticket-system/.claude/settings.json returns 0.

criteria.statement: Every audit run (including the hard-gate self-check) appends one JSON line to .foreman/tessguard-audit-log.jsonl; the self-check asserts core.hooksPath == .githooks and compares both shims' live sha256 against an EXPECTED_SHIM_SHAS mapping defined inside tessguard's own gated code.

gitgate.check_gate resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (never the operator-supplied audit root layer 1 uses) and requires at least one real TESSERA-write event (same 5 types, same any-of aggregation as layer 1) for the repo's registered project(s) within a trailing 24h wall-clock window.

A repo that resolves to zero registered TESSERA projects BLOCKS under gitgate (the deliberate inverse of layer 1's fail-open on the same input) -- an empty project set is vacuously false under any-of and blocking is the correct direction for a hard gate.
gitgate.main() returns exit code 0 on pass, non-zero on block, with a stderr message naming which project(s) were checked, the window, and the exact tessera command to fix it.

.githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are two-line exec shims only (exec python3 -m tessera.tessguard.gitgate); all real logic lives in gitgate.py, which is gated by goals_freeze_gate.py -- the shims themselves are not, since .githooks/ is excluded by component_coupling.py's dotdir predicate.
criteria.verification: wc -l /Users/m5/dev/ticket-system/.githooks/pre-commit /Users/m5/dev/ticket-system/.githooks/pre-push shows <=2 non-comment lines each; grep confirms both exec into tessera.tessguard.gitgate.

criteria.statement: Zero changes to tessera/store, tessera/api, tessera/gitops, tessera/reviewui, tessera/common -- every call is read-only against store's existing public methods (list_projects, get_project, get_events_since) and common's utc_now_iso().
criteria.verification: git diff --stat <pre-tessguard-sha>..HEAD -- tessera/store tessera/api tessera/gitops tessera/reviewui tessera/common produces empty output.

criteria.statement: gitgate is demonstrated end to end against a real, disposable git repository (not only a mocked Store): a real commit with zero real TESSERA activity in-window is blocked, and the same repo's commit succeeds once real activity exists.
criteria.verification: python3 -m unittest tessera.tessguard.tests.test_gitgate.GitgateTests.test_e2e_real_repo_block_then_pass exits 0 (constructs a temp git repo + temp tessera.db fixture, no mocks on the git or DB layer).

failure_criteria.statement: A layer-1 input failure (bad DB path, absent transcript, unreadable file) fails open -- reads as 'zero registered projects, nothing to flag' instead of a distinct error outcome.
failure_criteria.detection: C6's test asserts the missing-DB-path case produces an outcome distinguishable from a real clean pass, not just that no exception propagates.

failure_criteria.statement: gitgate fails open on an internal error (DB unreachable, git command fails) instead of blocking -- the exact asymmetry named in ARCHITECTURE.md between layer 1 (fails open) and layer 2 (must fail closed) collapses.
failure_criteria.detection: test_gitgate includes a case where Store() raises or git rev-parse fails, asserting a non-zero exit, not a swallowed exception defaulting to pass.

failure_criteria.statement: A number in this component's docstrings/README (event type counts, the 24h window, path-matching examples) appears with no reproduction path back to ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md or a test.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the diff for numeric claims in comments/docstrings; each must cite the test or review finding it traces to.

failure_criteria.statement: gitgate.py or audit.py assumes data/tessera.db exists relative to repo root without checking, producing a raw traceback instead of a legible error naming the fix.
failure_criteria.detection: C6/C9's tests include a missing-DB case asserting a clear, actionable message, not a bare stack trace.

failure_criteria.statement: The EXPECTED_SHIM_SHAS self-check (C8) is described as enforcement when goals_freeze_gate.py opens permanently after freeze and doesn't gate MultiEdit/NotebookEdit at all -- the docstring must state this is detection-friction, not a guarantee, matching ARCHITECTURE.md's own honest framing.
failure_criteria.detection: Code comment/docstring on the self-check cites the same limitation ARCHITECTURE.md names, not a stronger claim.

out_of_scope: N-project rollout: config-driven tessera.db path resolution for repos whose source_root lives outside ticket-system, per-project .githooks templating, canary sequencing across the other 20+ registered projects -- separate follow-up ticket.
Defeating `git commit --no-verify` -- no server-side git remote exists in this local-only setup to add a second enforcement point.
Cross-repo drift detection -- a session whose real writes land in a different repo than the one audited (VALE's measured case) is out of a per-repo check's scope by design.
Concurrent-session attribution -- store has no session id, only actor strings; two simultaneous sessions in one repo cannot be told apart by this design.
Automatic, non-time-based session-completion detection -- v1 requires an explicit, operator-named transcript; no wall-clock/cron auto-trigger.
Per-call (specific-edit-to-specific-ticket-write) pairing -- both layers operate at whole-session/whole-window granularity, never pairing an individual Edit to an individual TESSERA write.
Auto-filing tickets or posting comments from audit findings -- v1 writes to a local JSONL log only; wiring to any notification/auto-remediation channel is future work.

Self-selection mitigation -- the audit is invoked by the party it audits; a session that drifted is disproportionately the session nobody remembers to run it on. Named honestly in ARCHITECTURE.md, not solved here.
constraints: Python 3.9+ stdlib only, plus tessera.store and tessera.common -- no new dependency.
No changes to tessera/store, tessera/api, tessera/gitops, tessera/reviewui, tessera/common.
gitgate.main() must be safely invocable with cwd=repo_root and no environment assumptions beyond TESSGUARD_DB_PATH.
Dogfood scope only: built, tested, and validated against /Users/m5/dev/ticket-system. Not installed or exercised against any other registered project in this pass.
